precepts.text: Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you. We always skip that part: known among your tribes. Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise. So he took the chief of the tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over the people: captains over thousands, captains over hundreds, captains over fifties, captains over tens, and officers among the tribes. We are not making this structure up.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Paul was not there in Laodicea, yet he was with them in spirit, “joying and beholding your order”. God loves order, and the order of Israel is written: “Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.”

We always skip that part: “known among your tribes.” Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. That is not something done to them; they decided to hide and be known only locally, and made themselves a nobody. How will we know you are wise and understanding? No brother has been held back from teaching the morning daily bread. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise: this brother is good, I listen to his classes, he travels, he's here one week and there another month.

“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do. So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” So we are not making this structure up. The captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens are in the law.

That is why IUIC is restructuring. Some men have positions and don't fit the bill: authority without wisdom, no knowledge, not knowing how to build men. The scripture calls for wise men, understanding, and known.

precepts.text: Have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
precepts.point: Something you might not know: in the judge's chambers there are books on the wall, and those books have old cases. Your case might have the same case from 20 years ago. This is why the judge says, I'll be back with my decision. Some lawyers and prosecutors base their case on old cases. Where am I going with this? A judge is not always right. This is why they keep records, old records, so they can make the decision the right way. Some of you got a bishop in your camp, a captain in your camp, high ranking officers in your camp, and what did you do? You hide from them. These men are supposed to be your old records. And you know where you find the old records? The scriptures. Those are our records. When you ask Bishop a question, Bishop never gives you his opinion; he goes to the old records and makes them new to you. Where do you find the prophecies? In the old records.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.text: The respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration because of advantage: there's something you're going to gain by showing favoritism. And the end result: you are become judges of evil thoughts. Some brothers are horrible judges because there's something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them: they give you gifts, they're your ride to Sabbath, they got you a job. Now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord said that's an evil thing.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

precepts.text: Captains over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officers among the tribes, charged to judge righteously and not respect persons, for the judgment is God's.
precepts.point: Judgment did not pass away with the Old Testament. He that is spiritual judgeth all things, and the spiritual man is the man that keeps the commandments. The saints shall judge the world, so brethren should judge the smallest matters among themselves instead of going to law before the unjust; only matters of life and death under today's system go outside.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Moses recounts how Jethro’s counsel was put in place: “So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” These are the rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. This is the structure of righteous leadership the Most High established: captains and officers over the tribes, offices never heard in the church.

Then the charge to the judges: “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”. The men set over the people had to be such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness, because the judgment they gave was God’s.

Then the hard cases: “the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.” That is the order Jethro gave: every great matter to Moses, every small matter judged by the rulers. It is the same today. The hard matters go to the high-ranking officers and ultimately the bishop, while the smaller matters are judged by the lower-ranking officers.

precepts.text: Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's.
precepts.point: Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.” Basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut.

And “neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people’s opinion in a different direction. The judges were charged, “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”.

The judgment is God’s. Whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God.

precepts.text: Judge righteously between every man and his brother; ye shall not respect persons in judgment, but hear the small as well as the great.
precepts.point: In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.” This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged, “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”.

In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The small was heard as well as the great.

The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

precepts.text: The fourth generation would come hither again, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full; Sihon fell when it was full.
precepts.point: By this point their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay Sihon their king.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
When the Lord told Abraham his seed would serve four hundred years, he set the time of their return by the Amorites: “But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.” Israel could not come back into the land until the iniquity of the Amorites was full.

By the time Moses declares this law, it was. Their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay “Sihon the king of the Amorites, which dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan”. That is why the law is declared “After he had slain Sihon”: the fourth generation had come hither again, and Sihon fell when the iniquity of the Amorites was full.

precepts.text: The thing that thou doest is not good; thou wilt surely wear away, both thou and this people, for the thing is too heavy for one man.
precepts.point: His father in law told him the thing was not good: judging alone would wear away both Moses and the people. The counsel was to provide able men that fear God and set them in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
When Moses says “I am not able to bear you myself alone”, he is referring back to what his father in law saw in Exodus 18. Moses sat judging the people alone from morning until evening, the people waiting all day in line, because they came to him to inquire of God and to be shown the statutes and laws. His father in law told him: “The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.”

The Lord had multiplied Israel “as the stars of heaven for multitude”, and every one of them came with cumbrance, burden, and strife. One man judging all of that would wear away, and the people waiting on him would wear away with him. That is what Moses is asking: “How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?” The thing was too heavy for one man; it was not good, and it had to change.

precepts.text: Provide able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness, and place them as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
precepts.point: His father in law told him the thing was not good: judging alone would wear away both Moses and the people. The counsel was to provide able men that fear God and set them in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
The counsel of Moses' father in law was not only that the load was too heavy, but what to do about it: “Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens”. Able men that fear God, set in ranks over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, so the burden Moses could not bear alone was shared.

That is the answer to “How can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?” A people as the stars of heaven for multitude needs rulers over them, and they had to be a particular kind of men: fearing God, men of truth, hating covetousness. Moses is reminding Israel that the order set among them came from that counsel.

precepts.text: Do no unrighteousness in judgment; respect not the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty.
precepts.point: Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's: no tough face may intimidate or sway a verdict, because it is the Most High passing the judgment through the judge. The cause too hard goes up the chain to Moses, and that chain itself was instituted here.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour.” That is the same charge Moses gave the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. A poor man gets no pass for being poor, and a mighty man with money and possessions is not above the laws of the Most High; no one can buy himself out of judgment. Both are judged in righteousness.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”. No tough face may intimidate or sway a verdict, because it is the Most High passing the judgment through the judge. And the cause too hard for the judge goes up the chain: “the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it.” That chain itself was instituted here.

precepts.text: In nothing terrified by your adversaries, which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.
precepts.point: The principle still applies: the body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Fear of the adversary is a spirit the Most High never gave his people; whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“And in nothing terrified by your adversaries: which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.” That is the same command Moses gave Israel: “Dread not, neither be afraid of them. The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes”. The Amorites were no mightier than Egypt, and these same Israelites witnessed how the Lord broke Egypt to bring them out. Where was their faith?

The principle still applies. The body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Not being terrified is a token: to the adversaries, of their perdition, and to us, of salvation, and that of God. The Lord who bare Israel in the wilderness “as a man doth bear his son” goes before his people still, and fights for them.

precepts.text: God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
precepts.point: The principle still applies: the body still has adversaries that rise against it, and the command remains to be in nothing terrified by them. Fear of the adversary is a spirit the Most High never gave his people; whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” Fear of the adversary is a spirit, and the Most High never gave it to his people. When Israel dreaded the Amorites after all they had seen in Egypt and in the wilderness, that fear did not come from the Lord.

So whoever is terrified of the enemy is out of the Spirit. What the Lord gives is power, love, and a sound mind, and a sound mind remembers what he did in Egypt before our eyes and how he bare us in all the way that we went. “Dread not, neither be afraid of them” is not only a command; it is the Spirit the Most High actually gave.

precepts.text: Fear lest ye come short as the fathers did: the gospel was preached unto them as unto us, but the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.
precepts.point: The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. They had the word, the laws, the miracles, and the Lord going before them “in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day.” And “Yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God”.

That is the amazing part of this history: they saw all the miracles and were carried like a son, and still believed the Lord was setting them up to be killed by giants, when a giant has nothing on the Most High. The word did not profit them because it was not mixed with faith. They had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

So “Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.” The same promise is left to us, and the same way of coming short is open to us: hearing the word and not mixing it with faith.

precepts.text: The saints keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus; commandments and faith go together.
precepts.point: The fathers in the wilderness had the gospel preached to them as we have: deliverance from captivity into the promised kingdom. But the word did not profit them, not being mixed with faith; they had the laws without the faith, and it is impossible to have one without the other.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” Commandments and faith go together; the saints have both. Israel in the wilderness had the laws, but in this thing they did not believe the Lord their God, and the laws without the faith did not bring them into the land.

It is impossible to have one without the other. Keeping the commandments without believing the Lord who gave them is what the fathers did, and the word did not profit them. The saints keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, and that faith is what the fathers lacked when they would not believe the God who went before them in fire and cloud.

precepts.text: The Lord said speak ye unto the rock; Moses smote it twice in anger, and because he believed not, to sanctify the Lord in the eyes of Israel, he could not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes”: here is that history. At the waters the people fell into the same disbelief they had shown over and over, and the Lord told Moses, “Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water”. Speak to the rock.

Moses, in his anger, did not: “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice”. He called them rebels and smote the rock twice when the Lord had said to speak to it. The water still came out abundantly, but the judgment followed: “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.”

Moses failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, and his judgment was to be kept out of the land: “Thou also shalt not go in thither.” It was for their sakes, their unbelief, that he was provoked; but the failure was his, and leadership carries the greater condemnation. The more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

precepts.text: Be ye angry, and sin not; anger given room makes a man cast the commandments aside.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”. Anger itself is not the sin; but when anger takes hold, a man fails to apply what he knows. Moses knew the commandment: speak to the rock. In his anger at the people's disbelief he called them rebels and smote it twice. Anger lets the commandments slip.

That is how the Lord came to be angry with Moses for their sakes. Anger given room made him cast aside what the Lord had just told him, and he failed to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. Be angry and sin not: the anger may come, but the commandment has to stay in hand.

precepts.text: Moses and Elias appeared talking with Christ on the mount; Moses is good.
precepts.point: Moses is still good; he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount. He missed the promised land at that time, not the kingdom. But leadership carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.” Moses is still good. The judgment at the waters kept him out of the promised land at that time, but it did not keep him out of the kingdom: he stood with Elias before Christ on the mount, talking with him.

So “Thou also shalt not go in thither” was the loss of the land, not of the kingdom. But it stands as the warning for leadership, which carries the greater condemnation: the more given unto you, the more stripes when you fail, and Moses, who was given so much, missed the land for one failure at the rock.

precepts.text: They set at nought all his counsel and would none of his reproof; when the fear comes he laughs at the calamity, and they that call then are not answered, for they hated knowledge.
precepts.point: They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh”. That is Israel here. The Lord had given chance after chance to obey and not fear, and every time the same trial brought the same unbelief. His counsel was set at nought until the judgment fell; only then did they say “We have sinned against the Lord, we will go up and fight”.

Then they set his counsel at nought again. He said “Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies”, and they “went presumptuously up into the hill”, boldly doing what they were told not to do, as recorded in Numbers 14. The Amorites came out and chased them as bees do, and destroyed them in Seir unto Hormah: the fear came as desolation, and the destruction as a whirlwind.

“Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. So it was: “ye returned and wept before the Lord; but the Lord would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you.” When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late. They that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him, and so they abode in Kadesh many days.

precepts.text: Once the judgment is done, the apology does not undo it; the counsel had to be taken beforehand.
precepts.point: They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The advice was there the whole time: dread not, neither be afraid, the Lord your God shall fight for you. Israel would not take it, and the Lord sware that generation would not see the land. Only after the judgment fell did they want to repent, girding on every man his weapons of war and declaring themselves ready to go up.

Once the judgment is done, the apology does not undo it. “We have sinned against the Lord” and weeping before the Lord did not reverse what was sworn; the counsel had to be taken beforehand. Then they acted without advice a second time, going up when the Lord said go not up, and were chased as bees and destroyed unto Hormah. The counsel comes before the doing, and when the thing is once done, there is no repenting it back.

precepts.text: The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt.
precepts.point: God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes”. The Lord would go before us and fight our battles; that is what it means that he walketh in the midst of thy camp “to deliver thee, and to give up thine enemies before thee”.

And that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp: if he sees an unclean thing in thee he turns away from thee, and then the one who fights for you has turned away. Achan brought an unclean thing into the camp and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. So the camp was to be holy, for we are holy, and he who fights for us walks in it.

precepts.text: Judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger; ye shall not respect persons in judgment.
precepts.point: This goes back to Deuteronomy chapter 1, where the judges were charged to judge righteously between every man and his brother and the stranger with him, and to respect no persons in judgment.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

precepts.why:
“Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, fatherless, and widow.” This curse goes back to the beginning of Deuteronomy, where Moses charged the judges of Israel: “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.” The stranger that dwells with Israel is to have righteous judgment the same as an Israelite.

“Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”. A judge is not to be swayed by who stands before him, great or small, and not to fear any man's face, because the judgment belongs to the Most High. To pervert the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, the ones with nobody to stand up for them, is to respect persons, the very thing the judges were charged never to do. That is why the curse falls on it, and all the people say Amen.

points: Take you wise men: a judge must be wise. A stupid judge will destroy everything. That's why you must know the scriptures. If you a judge and you don't know the scriptures, you will eventually become a traitor.

And known among your tribes: a judge must be known. That is talking about reputation. Nobody just leaves law school and becomes a judge; some wait for years before they can be appointed. Before a president appoints a judge, he must know that judge's background, his reputation, and the cases he has been judging, because we got corrupt judges. And some of you are corrupt. We cannot have corrupt men ruling us.

And I will make them rulers over you. Why would he use that word rulers? To rule something means you got power over it. Some of you officers of 10: are you ready to rule 10 men? Can you even rule yourself? Can you rule your own household?

Something you might not know: in the judge's chambers there are books on the wall, and those books have old cases. Your case might have the same case from 20 years ago. This is why the judge says, I'll be back with my decision. Some lawyers and prosecutors base their case on old cases. Where am I going with this? A judge is not always right. This is why they keep records, old records, so they can make the decision the right way. Some of you got a bishop in your camp, a captain in your camp, high ranking officers in your camp, and what did you do? You hide from them. These men are supposed to be your old records. And you know where you find the old records? The scriptures. Those are our records. When you ask Bishop a question, Bishop never gives you his opinion; he goes to the old records and makes them new to you. Where do you find the prophecies? In the old records.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: Captains over thousands, captains over hundreds, captains over fifties, captains over tens, and officers among your tribes: those are judges. If you an officer of 10, you should be able to lead 10 men with no problem. If you're a captain of 100, you should be able to lead 100 men with no problem. And an officer of 10 should mentor with the man he wants to become like: the officer of 20 is the only one who can help you become that. Some of you used to be in the military and understand the ranking system, but when you come into the Most High God's military, you have no idea.

Expand your mind. We just traveled all over the continent of Africa, all over the Caribbean, South America, Europe, for Passover. Some camps have hundreds of men. Imagine you end up in one of those places: can you lead those 100 men? Be honest with yourself. Those brothers and sisters are not asking; they are going to look at you like that's the man that the bishop sent. You're the representation of the bishop, the deacons, the captains. When they see you come over there and they're confused by the way you move, they know something is wrong, and it's because of your lack of study. They're going to assume you've been around Bishop, you've been around deacons, you're the man; but then you get there and it's a totally different story.

points: Your reputation is how you deal with your wife, how you deal with your children, how you deal with the brother that sits next to you, your reputation in the congregation, and your reputation in your workplace. That means you faking it somewhere, and more than likely you faking it here, cuz your spirit agrees with out there. You only a judge when you among us, but in the streets you that same old person. Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously. Some of you are not judging righteously. To judge righteously you must be just, not partial. Some of you want the position to destroy brothers.

points: Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; ye shall hear the small as well as the great: you got to hear both sides, the small matter and the great matter.

Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man. You are not here to be loved, to be liked. You're judges. Some of you are afraid to make a decision because you afraid of what that man is going to think of you. You ain't here to make friends. This is why some of you are going to find yourself out of here: because when judgment happens to your friend, you're going to get offended. What does that have to do with you? Don't be afraid of men. Your fear is supposed to be toward the Most High, not those men. For the judgment is God's.

And the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it. Leaders, read that again slowly. You might have a situation where, to judge a matter, you don't know what to do.
